questions.question: An older adult has a progressive short-stepped broad-based gait, urinary urgency and dysexecutive cognitive impairment. MRI shows ventriculomegaly, enlarged Sylvian fissures and tight high-convexity sulci. Which diagnosis should be specifically evaluated?
options: Vascular parkinsonism as proven by a short-stepped gait alone
Hydrocephalus ex vacuo as established by ventricular enlargement alone
Typical amnestic AD as the only explanation
Idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus
questions.explanation:
Recognizing Idiopathic Normal-Pressure Hydrocephalus

Correct answer: Idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus

Clinical and Imaging Pattern

**iNPH is commonly gait led**, with cognitive slowing/executive dysfunction and urinary urgency or incontinence developing in variable combinations. The complete triad is neither necessary at first presentation nor sufficient by itself.

Ventriculomegaly is often quantified by an Evans index at least 0.3, but the overall pattern and alternative explanations matter. DESH denotes disproportionate CSF-space enlargement with tight high-convexity/midline sulci and enlarged Sylvian fissures.

Distinguish idiopathic disease from secondary hydrocephalus after hemorrhage, meningitis or another identified cause.

Selection for Further Assessment

**Exclude important gait, urinary and cognitive mimics** and assess objective baseline performance before CSF-drainage testing or shunt discussion.

The 2021 Japanese framework uses probable-category CSF pressure at or below ==200 mmH2O== with normal contents plus specified supporting clinical/imaging or drainage-response evidence; the name alone is not a guarantee that every pressure measurement is identical.

Potential benefit must be balanced with shunt risks and coexisting AD/vascular disease. A radiological pattern supports selection but does not promise complete cognitive recovery.

Vascular parkinsonism as proven by a short-stepped gait alone: Vascular disease can produce gait/executive impairment, but gait appearance alone does not resolve the differential; the characteristic CSF-space distribution supports iNPH evaluation.

Hydrocephalus ex vacuo as established by ventricular enlargement alone: Atrophy can enlarge ventricles, but disproportionate Sylvian enlargement with high-convexity tightness supports a hydrocephalic pattern rather than simple diffuse ex-vacuo enlargement.

Typical amnestic AD as the only explanation: AD can coexist, but a gait-led syndrome with this CSF-space pattern warrants iNPH assessment rather than an exclusively amnestic attribution.

questions.question: A patient develops rapidly progressive cognitive decline, ataxia and myoclonus. MRI shows cortical ribboning and caudate/putaminal diffusion abnormalities. Which CSF assay most specifically supports a prion etiology?
options: CSF 14-3-3 protein
Real-time quaking-induced conversion
CSF total tau
Serum neurofilament light chain
questions.explanation:
Suspected Sporadic CJD

Correct answer: Real-time quaking-induced conversion

Prion-Seeding Evidence

**RT-QuIC detects seeding activity of abnormal prion protein** and has high specificity in the appropriate syndrome. A progressive neuropsychiatric disorder with positive RT-QuIC can support probable sporadic CJD under the CDC framework.

Characteristic MRI includes caudate/putamen high signal or at least two cortical regions among temporal, parietal and occipital areas on DWI/FLAIR in the conventional criteria.

EEG periodic sharp-wave complexes and CSF injury markers can add support but may be absent or nonspecific. A negative test requires interpretation with sampling, subtype and the complete presentation.

Do Not Miss Treatable Mimics

**Autoimmune/infectious encephalitis, seizures, toxic-metabolic disease and malignancy** can cause rapid cognitive decline or diffusion abnormalities. Complete a targeted reversible-cause evaluation.

Definite CJD requires appropriate neuropathological confirmation. Seek specialist/prion surveillance advice for diagnosis, counselling and instrument/tissue precautions when relevant.

Care includes symptom relief, swallowing/nutrition decisions, family support and advance planning. Do not infer a curative treatment from a positive assay or use nonspecific 14-3-3 elevation alone to stop the mimic evaluation.

CSF 14-3-3 protein: 14-3-3 supports neuronal injury in an appropriate rapid syndrome but can rise in nonprion disease; it is less etiologically specific than RT-QuIC.

CSF total tau: Marked tau elevation indicates neuronal injury and can add support, but is not a prion-seeding assay and is less specific than RT-QuIC.

Serum neurofilament light chain: Neurofilament light reflects axonal injury across many conditions; it cannot specifically identify a prion cause of this syndrome.

questions.question: An older adult develops subacute memory loss, hyponatremia and dozens of very brief unilateral face–arm dystonic events daily. Which antibody-associated disorder is particularly likely?
options: LGI1-associated autoimmune encephalitis
Anti-NMDA-receptor encephalitis
GAD65-associated epilepsy as the most specific explanation
Sporadic CJD established from any brief involuntary movement
questions.explanation:
LGI1 Cognitive Disease and Brief Face–Arm Seizures

Correct answer: LGI1-associated autoimmune encephalitis

Faciobrachial Dystonic Seizures

**FBDS are brief, frequent, stereotyped face–arm events** strongly associated with LGI1 antibodies. They can precede a limbic cognitive syndrome, and a routine scalp EEG may not show a clear correlate for every event.

Hyponatremia and medial temporal abnormalities can support the syndrome, but normal early MRI or routine CSF does not exclude it.

Use antigen-specific testing and interpret serum/CSF results with the phenotype. A nonspecific historical VGKC-complex result is not interchangeable with confirmed LGI1 or CASPR2 antibodies.

Time-Sensitive Treatment

**Early immunotherapy is associated with better seizure control and reduced cognitive progression in cohort evidence.** Antiseizure medication alone may inadequately control FBDS.

Evaluate infection and other causes promptly, then consider specialist-directed corticosteroids, IVIG or plasma exchange according to the presentation and contraindications. Correct sodium carefully and monitor seizures and autonomic/behavioral complications.

The 103-patient study supports early recognition but is not randomized proof of one universally optimal regimen. Follow cognition and relapse risk after acute improvement rather than assuming seizure cessation guarantees complete memory recovery.

Anti-NMDA-receptor encephalitis: NMDA-receptor disease can cause memory, psychiatric and seizure syndromes, often with characteristic movement/autonomic evolution, but this brief faciobrachial phenotype is particularly associated with LGI1.

GAD65-associated epilepsy as the most specific explanation: GAD65 disease can produce epilepsy and other neurological autoimmunity, but the distinctive frequent face–arm dystonic seizures and hyponatremia point more strongly toward LGI1.

Sporadic CJD established from any brief involuntary movement: CJD can cause myoclonus and rapid decline, but this stereotyped seizure pattern with hyponatremia raises a treatable antibody-mediated disease that must be assessed.

questions.question: Which combination meets the 2016 clinical framework for possible autoimmune encephalitis, after reasonable exclusion of alternatives?
options: An amnestic syndrome only after a positive antibody returns
Years of isolated stable forgetfulness plus an incidental low-titre serum antibody
Any positive antibody result regardless of symptoms or assay specificity
Subacute memory/mental-status or psychiatric change plus at least one qualifying focal, seizure, CSF or MRI feature
questions.explanation:
Possible Autoimmune Encephalitis

Correct answer: Subacute memory/mental-status or psychiatric change plus at least one qualifying focal, seizure, CSF or MRI feature

Three Required Elements

**Possible AE requires subacute progression over less than three months** of working-memory deficits, altered mental status or psychiatric symptoms, plus at least one qualifying supporting feature.

Supporting features are a new focal CNS finding, seizures not explained by a previously known seizure disorder, CSF pleocytosis ==above 5 cells/µL== or MRI findings suggestive of encephalitis.

Reasonable exclusion of alternative causes is also required. Possible is a probability level, not proof that every case has an autoimmune etiology.

Investigation and Treatment Sequence

**MRI, EEG and CSF** help assess inflammatory, infectious and seizure-related causes. Send appropriate antibody tests in serum and CSF as indicated by the suspected syndrome.

HSV and other infections require urgent consideration and empiric treatment when indicated; an early negative PCR can be falsely reassuring. Do not let an autoimmune label delay pathogen-directed treatment.

After appropriate exclusion/treatment of infection and other mimics, immunotherapy can be initiated in a strongly supported syndrome without waiting indefinitely for antibody results. Escalation and tumor screening are tailored to phenotype, antibody and response.

For severe supported adult AE, Canadian consensus recommends high-dose IV methylprednisolone, for example ==1 g daily for five days==, combined with IVIG totaling ==2 g/kg over two to five days== or a suitable plasma-exchange course. Contraindications, infection exclusion and phenotype determine the choice; nonresponse may prompt second-line therapy such as rituximab.

An amnestic syndrome only after a positive antibody returns: The 2016 framework deliberately permits a clinical possible diagnosis before antibody results, allowing timely evaluation and appropriately selected treatment.

Years of isolated stable forgetfulness plus an incidental low-titre serum antibody: The possible-AE framework requires a compatible subacute clinical syndrome and supporting features; a discordant low-positive antibody does not replace that clinical requirement.

Any positive antibody result regardless of symptoms or assay specificity: Antibody testing can be misleading when pretest probability is low; interpretation requires phenotype, specimen and assay validation.

questions.question: A 23-year-old woman develops rapidly progressive psychosis, reduced speech, seizures, orofacial dyskinesia and autonomic instability. Infectious evaluation and treatment are proceeding. Which investigation most directly supports the suspected antibody-mediated diagnosis?
options: CSF CASPR2-IgG testing as the leading phenotype-specific assay
CSF LGI1-IgG testing as the leading phenotype-specific assay
CSF GABA-B-receptor antibodies as the leading phenotype-specific assay
CSF IgG antibodies against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor
questions.explanation:
NMDAR Encephalitis: A Psychiatric–Neurological Evolution

Correct answer: CSF IgG antibodies against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor

Recognizing the Syndrome

**Anti-NMDAR encephalitis** can evolve from psychiatric/cognitive symptoms to speech dysfunction, seizures, dyskinesia/rigidity, reduced consciousness and autonomic dysfunction or hypoventilation.

The 2016 probable framework uses rapid onset within three months of at least four of six symptom groups plus abnormal EEG or inflammatory CSF and reasonable exclusion of alternatives; a compatible three-group presentation with a teratoma can also meet that pathway.

Definite antibody-associated disease requires the appropriate clinical context and IgG anti-GluN1 evidence. CSF testing is essential when suspicion is high; a serum-only result should not substitute for a careful evaluation.

Treatment and Tumor Assessment

**Search for an associated tumor, especially ovarian teratoma in the relevant population**, and arrange treatment/removal when indicated. Age and sex influence the screening plan but do not alone confirm or exclude the disease.

After reasonable infection exclusion, prompt first-line immunotherapy commonly combines corticosteroids with IVIG or plasma exchange in severe disease. Rituximab or another second-line strategy may be considered for inadequate response under specialist care.

Seizure, airway, dysautonomia, nutrition and rehabilitation needs can be substantial. Recovery may be prolonged, and early psychiatric symptoms should not prevent neurological reassessment when the syndrome evolves.

CSF CASPR2-IgG testing as the leading phenotype-specific assay: CASPR2 disease can produce limbic symptoms, peripheral hyperexcitability and Morvan features; it is a genuine differential but less characteristic than NMDAR disease for this presentation.

CSF LGI1-IgG testing as the leading phenotype-specific assay: LGI1 disease commonly presents later in life with limbic memory dysfunction, hyponatremia and faciobrachial dystonic seizures; the psychiatric–speech–dyskinesia–autonomic evolution here particularly suggests NMDAR disease.

CSF GABA-B-receptor antibodies as the leading phenotype-specific assay: GABA-B disease can cause severe seizures and limbic encephalitis, often with a tumor association, but the broader psychiatric, speech and movement evolution here is more characteristic of NMDAR encephalitis.

questions.question: A malnourished patient with prolonged vomiting has confusion, gaze-evoked nystagmus and gait ataxia. Which immediate treatment principle is appropriate?
options: Use oral low-dose supplementation as the only acute treatment despite vomiting
Wait for the serum thiamine result before treatment
Give parenteral thiamine promptly and correct associated metabolic problems
Withhold urgent glucose for hypoglycemia until a thiamine infusion is available
questions.explanation:
Suspected Wernicke Encephalopathy

Correct answer: Give parenteral thiamine promptly and correct associated metabolic problems

Clinical Recognition

**Wernicke encephalopathy** results from thiamine deficiency and can occur with alcohol-associated malnutrition, hyperemesis, bariatric complications and other prolonged nutritional deficits.

The full confusion–ocular–ataxia triad is often absent. In a relevant context, two of dietary deficiency, ocular signs, cerebellar dysfunction and altered mental state/memory support clinical suspicion.

A normal MRI or an incomplete triad does not safely exclude the diagnosis. Delayed treatment can lead to persistent amnestic/Korsakoff deficits.

Dose Framework and Support

**EFNS recommends thiamine ==200 mg IV three times daily==**, preferably before carbohydrate when feasible, continued according to clinical response. Other national protocols use higher regimens, so identify and follow the applicable protocol.

Do not delay emergency glucose for a hypoglycemic patient; provide thiamine immediately alongside or as soon as available. Check and correct magnesium, which is relevant to thiamine-dependent function.

Treat refeeding risk, electrolyte deficits and the underlying nutritional cause. Monitor response and provide ongoing nutritional rehabilitation rather than assuming a single injection completes treatment.

UK acute-hospital alcohol guidance uses IV thiamine ==300–500 mg three times daily== for three to five days with daily review for suspected/established Wernicke disease. This higher regimen and the older EFNS 200-mg regimen are explicitly different protocol frameworks, not interchangeable claims of one universal dose.

Use oral low-dose supplementation as the only acute treatment despite vomiting: Oral absorption and intake are unreliable in this setting; suspected acute Wernicke disease requires parenteral treatment rather than a maintenance-only approach.

Wait for the serum thiamine result before treatment: Laboratory confirmation can be delayed or imperfect, while untreated deficiency can cause irreversible injury; a compatible high-risk presentation warrants prompt treatment.

Withhold urgent glucose for hypoglycemia until a thiamine infusion is available: Thiamine should be given promptly, ideally before or with carbohydrate when feasible, but lifesaving correction of hypoglycemia must not be delayed.

questions.question: A patient with two years of progressive cognitive decline has low B12 and a substantial anticholinergic medication burden. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
options: Treat the deficiencies and medication burden while reassessing for coexisting neurodegenerative or vascular disease
Treat presumed AD alone and defer the contributor review
Attribute the complete two-year syndrome to B12 deficiency and end etiologic follow-up
Reduce medicines without treating B12 or investigating its cause
questions.explanation:
Reversible Contributors Are Not Always the Sole Cause

Correct answer: Treat the deficiencies and medication burden while reassessing for coexisting neurodegenerative or vascular disease

Contributor Versus Complete Explanation

**Medication toxicity, B12 deficiency, thyroid dysfunction, sleep disorders and systemic illness** can worsen cognitive performance and daily function.

Assess whether the degree, timing and phenotype plausibly match the abnormality. A common laboratory finding is not automatically the sole cause of a prolonged progressive syndrome.

B12 deficiency can produce neurological disease without a prominent anemia; confirm and treat according to the clinical setting and investigate the cause.

Deprescribing and Follow-up

**Review anticholinergics, sedatives and interacting drugs**, prioritizing agents with weak indications or clear cognitive effects. Use a taper when required and monitor the symptoms for which a medicine was prescribed.

Correct identified nutritional/metabolic abnormalities and reassess cognition and function after an appropriate interval. Persistent decline warrants continued etiologic evaluation.

HIV, syphilis or other infection testing is selected by presentation and risk rather than ordered indiscriminately or categorically omitted. Maintain a mixed-cause formulation when several contributing processes remain supported.

Treat presumed AD alone and defer the contributor review: AD can coexist, but treating a suspected primary degeneration does not address a correctable B12 deficit or harmful anticholinergic burden.

Attribute the complete two-year syndrome to B12 deficiency and end etiologic follow-up: B12 disease can cause cognitive and neurological impairment, but the duration and coexistence of other pathology require reassessment rather than a guaranteed single-cause conclusion.

Reduce medicines without treating B12 or investigating its cause: Deprescribing is useful, but does not replace correction and etiologic investigation of a documented deficiency that may contribute to neurological injury.

questions.question: A patient with dementia becomes agitated mainly during bathing. Assessment identifies painful shoulder movement and frightening rapid handling; there is no immediate danger. Which initial plan is best?
options: Begin an antipsychotic before addressing the painful care trigger
Treat pain and adapt the care approach and environment before considering an antipsychotic
Schedule a benzodiazepine for each bath as the first intervention
Increase the cholinesterase-inhibitor dose as the immediate solution
questions.explanation:
Agitation: Treat Distress and Triggers First

Correct answer: Treat pain and adapt the care approach and environment before considering an antipsychotic

Identify the Meaning of the Behavior

**Pain, delirium, constipation, retention, sensory impairment, fear and unmet needs** commonly drive agitation. Obtain a specific description of timing, triggers and consequences.

Use a calm pace, explanation, familiar carers, privacy, sensory support and a tolerable care routine. Evaluate medical causes when behavior changes abruptly.

Nonpharmacological care is active treatment, not simply postponement of medication.

Restricted Medication Role

**Consider an antipsychotic only for an appropriate severe-distress or harm-risk indication**, after reviewing benefits, risks, alternatives and the possibility of DLB/parkinsonian sensitivity.

Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest appropriate period, define a target behavior and reassess regularly. NICE advises at least six-weekly review and stopping if there is no clear ongoing benefit.

Drug approvals differ by jurisdiction and indication; an approval for AD-associated agitation does not make a medicine an unrestricted as-needed sedative for every dementia behavior. Continue pain, environmental and caregiver interventions even if medication becomes necessary.

Begin an antipsychotic before addressing the painful care trigger: Medication may be needed for severe distress or harm risk in selected cases, but the identified pain and handling trigger should be addressed first in this non-dangerous situation.

Schedule a benzodiazepine for each bath as the first intervention: Short-term sedation has selected uses, but routine pre-bath benzodiazepines add falls/confusion risks while leaving the modifiable distress mechanism untreated.

Increase the cholinesterase-inhibitor dose as the immediate solution: A cholinesterase inhibitor may have a role in the underlying dementia, but dose escalation is not an immediate treatment for pain and frightening handling during bathing.

questions.question: A patient with mild dementia can explain a proposed treatment and its main consequences but has begun getting lost while driving. Which principle is most appropriate?
options: Assess treatment-decision capacity and driving safety separately using the relevant functional evidence
The dementia diagnosis automatically removes capacity for every decision
A single cognitive-screen cutoff determines both consent capacity and driving fitness universally
Preserved conversational fluency proves safe driving despite navigation failures
questions.explanation:
Capacity and Driving Need Functional Assessment

Correct answer: Assess treatment-decision capacity and driving safety separately using the relevant functional evidence

Supported Decision-Making

**Assess the particular decision** using understanding, retention, use/weighing of information and communication under the applicable legal framework. Treat delirium and optimize hearing, language and presentation of information.

A patient may retain capacity for a simple treatment while needing support for finances or a more complex choice. Document the assessment rather than substituting a global label.

Respect autonomy and involve family or legally authorized support as appropriate, while distinguishing support from automatic transfer of every decision.

Practical Safety

**Driving requires navigation, attention, judgement, vision and motor function.** Getting lost, crashes, near misses and informant concerns warrant prompt advice and appropriate driving evaluation.

Licensing/reporting obligations are jurisdiction specific and must be checked locally. Avoid presenting a foreign legal rule as universally applicable.

Also review medication administration, cooking, finances, falls and vulnerability to exploitation. Use proportionate supports that preserve participation and reduce concrete risks rather than assuming every activity must stop at diagnosis.

The dementia diagnosis automatically removes capacity for every decision: Capacity is decision specific and can vary with complexity, support and time; a diagnosis alone does not establish global incapacity.

A single cognitive-screen cutoff determines both consent capacity and driving fitness universally: Screen scores can inform concern, but no universal number resolves all decisions or driving tasks across individuals and jurisdictions.

Preserved conversational fluency proves safe driving despite navigation failures: Social conversation can remain fluent while visuospatial, executive or navigation skills are impaired; concrete driving concerns require their own assessment.

questions.question: An older adult at increased risk of cognitive decline asks what the 2025 US POINTER trial demonstrated. Which answer is most accurate?
options: It demonstrated a lower lifetime incidence of all dementia as its primary endpoint
A structured multidomain lifestyle intervention improved the global cognitive composite more than a self-guided intervention over two years
It showed the independent effect of exercise by holding all other components identical
It established a treatment that reverses established Alzheimer dementia
questions.explanation:
Risk Reduction Without Overstating Prevention

Correct answer: A structured multidomain lifestyle intervention improved the global cognitive composite more than a self-guided intervention over two years

Randomized Evidence

**US POINTER enrolled 2111 at-risk older adults** and compared a structured higher-intensity programme with a lower-intensity self-guided programme.

The structured group had a statistically greater rate of improvement in the global cognitive composite, with an adjusted between-group difference of ==0.029 SD per year== over two years.

Both groups improved on the measured composite. The result does not establish cure, reversal of established dementia or guaranteed lifetime prevention.

Clinical Counselling

**Recommend feasible physical activity, vascular-risk care, a healthy dietary pattern and cognitive/social engagement**, with hearing/vision support and other individual needs addressed.

Adapt recommendations to mobility, frailty, cardiac status and access rather than giving one rigid exercise prescription to every patient.

Avoid claiming that a supplement, commercial brain game or blood biomarker test by itself prevents dementia. Risk modification can be worthwhile despite uncertainty about an individual outcome, and it complements rather than replaces evaluation of new cognitive symptoms.

It demonstrated a lower lifetime incidence of all dementia as its primary endpoint: The reported primary endpoint was a global cognitive-composite trajectory over two years, not lifetime dementia incidence.

It showed the independent effect of exercise by holding all other components identical: The structured intervention was multidomain; the design did not isolate exercise as the sole differing causal component.

It established a treatment that reverses established Alzheimer dementia: The trial enrolled at-risk older adults and assessed cognitive change; that is distinct from reversing established biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer dementia.
